title: Susan Collins on Roe v. Wade and the Next Justice

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日简报《DealBook》报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市的 DealBook 峰会上，现场采访商界、政界和文化界最具影响力的几位领袖，包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the DealBook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.en: You can watch some of these unguarded, unfiltered conversations as they happen.
sentences.zh: 您可以观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的实时对话。

sentences.en: We're going to be live-streaming select interviews for anyone to watch, free, at nytimes.com on November 18th.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我们将在 nytimes.com 上直播精选采访，供任何人免费观看。

sentences.en: If you're not already a subscriber, you can download the New York Times app to watch and get a month of free access to all of our journalism.
sentences.zh: 如果您还不是订阅者，您可以下载《纽约时报》应用程序进行观看，并获得我们所有新闻内容一个月的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望您能收看。

sentences.en: You won't want to miss it.
sentences.zh: 您一定不想错过。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Today.
sentences.zh: 今天。

sentences.en: When Justice Anthony Kennedy announced his retirement last week, attention immediately turned to the very small number of senators
sentences.zh: 上周安东尼·肯尼迪大法官宣布退休时，人们的注意力立即转向了极少数参议员，

sentences.en: who remain willing to break from their parties on major issues.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然愿意在重大问题上与自己的党派决裂。

sentences.en: We speak to one of them.
sentences.zh: 我们采访了其中一位。

sentences.en: Monday, July 2nd.
sentences.zh: 7月2日，星期一。

sentences.en: Some news just coming across right now from the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 最高法院刚刚传来一些消息。

sentences.en: After the final day of the term and a few hours after some of those final decisions, we have just learned that Justice Anthony Kennedy will be retiring.
sentences.zh: 在本届任期的最后一天，以及其中一些最后裁决做出几小时后，我们刚刚获悉安东尼·肯尼迪大法官将要退休。

sentences.en: Anthony Kennedy's retirement will set in motion the biggest change in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 安东尼·肯尼迪的退休将引发美国最高法院半个世纪以来最大的一次变动。

sentences.en: Supreme Court in half a century.
sentences.zh: 最高法院在半个世纪以来最大的一次变动。

sentences.en: That's because Kennedy has often been the most influential justice casting the deciding vote in closely divided cases.
sentences.zh: 这是因为肯尼迪往往是最有影响力的法官，在势均力敌的案件中投出决定性的一票。

sentences.en: I think without any question, this is the biggest moment of the Trump presidency.
sentences.zh: 我认为毫无疑问，这是特朗普总统任期内最重要的时刻。

sentences.en: We are going to be replacing a swing vote with someone who in all likelihood will be a conservative, a reliable conservative across the board.
sentences.zh: 我们将用一个极有可能是保守派的人来取代一个摇摆票，一个全面可靠的保守派。

sentences.en: This just changes the entire fundamental dynamic of the United States Supreme Court potentially for a generation.
sentences.zh: 这只是改变了美国最高法院的整个基本动态，可能长达一代人。

sentences.en: You are going to see 20 states pass laws banning abortion outright, just banning abortion,
sentences.zh: 你会看到20个州通过法律彻底禁止堕胎，仅仅是禁止堕胎，

sentences.en: because they know that there are now going to be five votes on the Supreme Court to overturn Roe v.
sentences.zh: 因为他们知道最高法院现在将有五票来推翻罗诉

sentences.en: Wade.
sentences.zh: 韦德案。

sentences.en: Roe v.
sentences.zh: 罗诉

sentences.en: Wade is doomed.
sentences.zh: 韦德案注定要完蛋了。

sentences.en: It is gone because Donald Trump won the election.
sentences.zh: 它已经不复存在了，因为唐纳德·特朗普赢得了大选。

sentences.en: Senator Collins, can you tell me where you were and how you first learned the news of Justice Kennedy's resignation?
sentences.zh: 柯林斯参议员，您能告诉我您当时在哪里，以及您是如何最初得知肯尼迪大法官辞职的消息的吗？

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I was attending a Republican lunch that's held every week, and toward the end of the lunch, Ted Cruz interrupted the discussion and said,
sentences.zh: 我当时正在参加每周举行一次的共和党午餐会，在午餐快结束时，泰德·克鲁兹打断了讨论并说，

sentences.en: Justice Kennedy has tendered his resignation.
sentences.zh: 肯尼迪大法官已经提交了他的辞呈。

sentences.en: He had been looking at his phone, and the news alert had come over.
sentences.zh: 他一直在看手机，然后新闻快讯就传过来了。

sentences.en: So there were exclamations of surprise, and each of us whipped out our own cell phones to find out what was going on and whether there were further details.
sentences.zh: 所以大家发出惊叹声，我们每个人都迅速掏出手机，想看看发生了什么，以及是否有更多细节。

sentences.en: I love this idea that all these senators are getting the news the same way that all the rest of us are.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这种想法，所有这些参议员获取新闻的方式和我们所有人一模一样。

sentences.en: That's for sure.
sentences.zh: 那是肯定的。

sentences.en: And funny that you should say that, because I called my staff, and I said, did you know this?
sentences.zh: 你这么说真搞笑，因为我给我的工作人员打电话，我说，你们知道这个吗？

sentences.en: And they said, the news is only nine seconds old.
sentences.zh: 他们说，这个新闻才刚出来九秒钟。

sentences.en: We didn't have time yet to alert you to it.
sentences.zh: 我们还没来得及提醒你。

sentences.en: Republican Senator Susan Collins spoke to us on Friday afternoon from her home in Maine.
sentences.zh: 共和党参议员苏珊·柯林斯于周五下午在缅因州的家中接受了我们的采访。

sentences.en: Well, so you might actually, and I'm sure this has dawned on you, you might actually be central to who the president chooses for the court.
sentences.zh: 那么，你可能实际上，而且我相信你已经意识到了，你实际上可能是总统为法院选择谁的关键人物。

sentences.en: Because, and this is the reason we wanted to talk to you today, you could find yourself becoming the key vote in all this.
sentences.zh: 因为，这也是我们今天想和你谈的原因，你可能会发现自己成为这一切中的关键一票。

sentences.en: So did you understand right away that you would immediately be a central figure in this, that all eyes would turn to you?
sentences.zh: 所以你当时是否立即明白，你将立即成为这其中的核心人物，所有的目光都会转向你？

sentences.en: Not really.
sentences.zh: 并没有。

sentences.en: I knew that I was going to be faced with a lot of pressure, no matter whom was appointed, and that it was going to be another huge issue on my plate.
sentences.zh: 我知道无论谁被任命，我都将面临巨大的压力，而且这将是我面前又一个巨大的议题。

sentences.en: But it was only when I returned from that lunch to my office and saw that my office was staked out with this mob, pardon the word, of reporters.
sentences.zh: 但只有当我从那场午餐会回到办公室，看到我的办公室被这群——原谅我用这个词——记者团团围住时，

sentences.en: And cameras that I thought, oh, no, here we go again.
sentences.zh: 还有摄像机，我才想，哦，不，又来了。

sentences.en: And I actually joked and said, I assume that you're here to talk about a bill that I have that I hope would help lower drug prices.
sentences.zh: 我甚至开玩笑说，我以为你们来是为了谈论我提出的一项希望有助于降低药品价格的法案。

sentences.en: Prescription drug prices.
sentences.zh: 处方药价格。

sentences.en: And they all laughed and immediately turned to the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 他们都笑了，然后立即把话题转向了最高法院。

sentences.en: So the reporters, the mob, had figured it out before you.
sentences.zh: 所以记者们，这群人，比你先弄明白了。

sentences.en: I must confess that that is true.
sentences.zh: 我必须承认那是真的。

sentences.en: I knew that this was going to be another huge issue.
sentences.zh: 我知道这将是另一个巨大的议题。

sentences.en: But it was only when I saw them all staked out at my office that I thought, oh, my goodness, they believe that I'm going to be a pivotal vote that could determine the outcome.
sentences.zh: 但直到我看到他们全部守候在我的办公室外，我才想，哦，天哪，他们相信我将成为能够决定结果的关键一票。

sentences.en: Even though, in my mind, there are several pivotal votes.
sentences.zh: 尽管在我看来，还有几个关键票。

sentences.en: There are some moderate Democrats who supported, for example, Justice Gorsuch's nomination and my friend Lisa Murkowski.
sentences.zh: 有一些温和派民主党人支持，例如，戈萨奇大法官的提名，还有我的朋友丽莎·穆尔科斯基。

sentences.en: But it was daunting.
sentences.zh: 但这令人畏惧。

sentences.en: Well, so like it or not, I think in the public's mind, the reason that you are so the focus of all this attention and interest and reporters outside your office,
sentences.zh: 好吧，不管你喜不喜欢，我认为在公众眼中，你之所以成为所有这些关注和兴趣的焦点以及你办公室外的记者的焦点，

sentences.en: and the same I'm sure is true of Senator Murkowski, is because you are both seen as willing to stand apart from your party, to be independent-minded.
sentences.zh: 我相信穆尔科斯基参议员也是如此，是因为你们俩都被视为愿意与你们的党派保持距离，具有独立思考能力。

sentences.en: But also, because you are both women Republicans.
sentences.zh: 而且，也是因为你们俩都是女性共和党人。

sentences.en: And for many people, this open seat is about one case, Roe v.
sentences.zh: 对很多人来说，这个空缺席位只关乎一个案件，即罗诉

sentences.en: Wade.
sentences.zh: 韦德案。

sentences.en: That's probably an accurate analysis.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一个准确的分析。

sentences.en: For the last, I think, five years, I have consistently been ranked as the most bipartisan member of the Senate.
sentences.zh: 在过去，我认为是五年里，我一直被评为参议院中最具两党合作精神的成员。

sentences.en: So clearly, my record shows that I'm willing to cross the aisle, that I don't vote a straight party line, and that I look at issues based on their merits.
sentences.zh: 所以很明显，我的记录表明我愿意跨越党派界限，我不按严格的党派路线投票，我根据事情本身的好坏来看待问题。

sentences.en: As far as Roe is concerned, there's no doubt that there are many people who are very concerned about what this means for a number of cases.
sentences.zh: 就罗诉韦德案而言，毫无疑问，许多人非常关心这对许多案件意味着什么。

sentences.en: And Roe v.
sentences.zh: 而罗诉

sentences.en: Wade is certainly one of them.
sentences.zh: 韦德案无疑是其中之一。

sentences.en: I think there are also people who are trying to make this all about Roe v.
sentences.zh: 我认为也有人在试图把这一切都归结为罗诉

sentences.en: Wade, even though the implications go far beyond that, since Justice Kennedy was considered the decisive vote on so many important issues.
sentences.zh: 韦德案，尽管其影响远远超出了这一点，因为肯尼迪大法官被认为是许多重要问题上的决定性投票人。

sentences.en: And indeed, Roe v.
sentences.zh: 事实上，罗诉

sentences.en: Wade wrote the landmark same-sex marriage case, for example.
sentences.zh: 韦德案确立了具有里程碑意义的同性婚姻案件等。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But for both sides of this debate, we know that abortion can be, and probably will be, a key issue and a deeply emotional issue.
sentences.zh: 但对于这场辩论的双方来说，我们都知道堕胎可以而且可能将是一个关键问题和一个深具情感色彩的问题。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: Senator, what is your position on abortion?
sentences.zh: 参议员，您对堕胎的立场是什么？

sentences.en: I am pro-choice.
sentences.zh: 我是支持堕胎权的。

sentences.en: I consider Roe v.
sentences.zh: 我认为罗诉

sentences.en: Wade to be settled law.
sentences.zh: 韦德案是已经尘埃落定的法律。

sentences.en: And what does that mean to you?
sentences.zh: 这对你意味着什么？

sentences.en: It means that it is a precedent that should be respected.
sentences.zh: 这意味着它是一个应该被尊重的先例。

sentences.en: Now, I do not apply a litmus test to the personal views of a judicial nominee,
sentences.zh: 现在，我不会对司法提名人的个人观点进行纯洁性测试，

sentences.en: because I know personally that you can have a personal opinion on what you would do in a certain difficult situation that may well differ from your public policy view.
sentences.zh: 因为我个人知道，对于你在某个困难情况下会做什么，你可能会有与你的公共政策观点截然不同的个人意见。

sentences.en: So, if a judge is pro-life personally, I respect that view.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果一个法官在个人立场上反对堕胎，我尊重这种观点。

sentences.en: But I also want that judge to be able to put aside his or her personal views and apply what is the longstanding precedent.
sentences.zh: 但我也希望这位法官能够抛开他或她个人的观点，并应用长期存在的先例。

sentences.en: And Roe v.
sentences.zh: 而罗诉

sentences.en: Wade is a longstanding precedent that has been reaffirmed by the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 韦德案是经最高法院多次重申的长期先例。

sentences.en: And here, Justice Kennedy played a key role in the Casey v.
sentences.zh: 在这里，肯尼迪大法官在凯西诉

sentences.en: Planned Parenthood case.
sentences.zh: 计划生育案中发挥了关键作用。

sentences.en: So, Senator, in thinking about a nominee to replace Justice Kennedy,
sentences.zh: 因此，参议员女士，在考虑替换肯尼迪大法官的提名人时，

sentences.en: are you saying that the way that you're going to be thinking about this is whether or not a possible justice respects the concept of legal precedent and that you see Roe v.
sentences.zh: 您是说您考虑这个问题的方式将是潜在的大法官是否尊重法律先例的概念，并且您认为罗诉

sentences.en: Wade as established legal precedent?
sentences.zh: 韦德案是既定的法律先例吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, you will be making your decision based on that rather than the personal view of the judge?
sentences.zh: 所以您将根据这一点而不是法官的个人观点来做出决定？

sentences.en: Yes, but I don't mean to imply that that's the only issue that matters to me in evaluating a nominee.
sentences.zh: 是的，但我并不是说这是我在评估提名人时唯一看重的问题。

sentences.en: I want to look at the person's qualifications, experience, whether they have the proper judicial temperament.
sentences.zh: 我想看看这个人的资质、经验，以及他们是否具备适当的司法气质。

sentences.en: There are a lot of other criteria that go into my decision-making.
sentences.zh: 还有很多其他标准进入我的决策过程中。

sentences.en: I should also mention that, obviously, if a nominee had demonstrated hostility toward Roe v.
sentences.zh: 我还应该提到，很明显，如果一个提名人在官方身份上表现出对罗诉

sentences.en: Wade in an official capacity, that that would cause me great concern.
sentences.zh: 韦德案的敌意，那会让我非常担忧。

sentences.en: In other words, if they had shown skepticism of the decision in their actions and in their legal rulings, that might be sufficient for you to vote against him or her.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果他们在行动和法律裁决中表现出对该裁决的怀疑，这可能就足以让你投反对票。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, is it accurate to say that you are pro-choice, but you are not making your decision for the next Supreme Court justice based on whether or not they are pro-choice,
sentences.zh: 那么，这样说是否准确：您支持堕胎权，但您对下一任最高法院大法官的选择并不是基于他们是否支持堕胎权，

sentences.en: but that you very much do not want Roe v.
sentences.zh: 而是您非常不希望罗诉

sentences.en: Wade to be overturned, and that will be a significant part of your thinking in considering any nominee?
sentences.zh: 韦德案被推翻，这将是您在考虑任何提名人时的一个重要考量？

sentences.en: That's accurate.
sentences.zh: 这很准确。

sentences.en: But how can you be sure, Senator, that respect for precedent equals respect for Roe?
sentences.zh: 但是参议员，您怎么能确信尊重先例就等于尊重罗诉韦德案呢？

sentences.en: The president has said that he thinks his appointments will result in Roe v.
sentences.zh: 总统曾表示，他认为他的任命将导致罗诉

sentences.en: Wade being overturned.
sentences.zh: 韦德案被推翻。

sentences.en: Well, I don't think the president's right about that.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为总统在这点上并不正确。

sentences.en: But I think, for example, that John Roberts, given his respect for precedent and his cautious approach, despite what personal views he may hold,
sentences.zh: 但我认为，例如，约翰·罗伯茨，鉴于他尊重先例和谨慎的态度，无论他抱有什么个人观点，

sentences.en: I would be very surprised if the chief justice would ever vote to overturn Roe v.
sentences.zh: 如果首席大法官投票推翻罗诉

sentences.en: Wade.
sentences.zh: 韦德案，我会感到非常惊讶。

sentences.en: Just to give you an example.
sentences.zh: 这只是给你举个例子。

sentences.en: Now, one of the dilemmas that one has when reviewing a judicial nominee is following the Ruth Bader Ginsburg precedent.
sentences.zh: 现在，审查司法提名人时面临的一个困境是遵循鲁斯·巴德·金斯伯格先例。
zh_words: 遵循鲁斯·巴德·金斯伯格

sentences.en: Judges will not tell you, nor should they tell you, how they would rule on a specific case.
sentences.zh: 法官不会告诉你，他们也不应该告诉你，他们会如何对一个具体的案件做出裁决。

sentences.en: And it's inappropriate for a member of Congress, a member of the Senate, to ask how a nominee would vote on a particular case.
sentences.zh: 国会议员、参议员要求提名人对特定案件如何投票是不合适的。

sentences.en: That compromises the ability of the judge to render an impartial decision based on the facts of the case that are presented to him or her later on.
sentences.zh: 这会损害法官根据随后提交给他的事实做出公正裁决的能力。

sentences.en: But you think the president is mistaken?
sentences.zh: 但你认为总统弄错了？

sentences.en: You think this court, even with a conservative judge replacing Justice Kennedy, will not overturn Roe v.
sentences.zh: 你认为这个法院，即使有一位保守派法官接替肯尼迪大法官，也不会推翻罗诉

sentences.en: Wade?
sentences.zh: 韦德案吗？

sentences.en: Well, I'm not saying that just any conservative judge would reach the conclusion that I think is most likely.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我并不是说任何保守派法官都会得出我认为最有可能的结论。

sentences.en: There are a couple of people who have been mentioned who have demonstrated hostility and an eagerness to overturn Roe v.
sentences.zh: 有几个人被提及，他们表现出了对罗诉

sentences.en: Wade.
sentences.zh: 韦德案的敌意和急于推翻它的急切心情。

sentences.en: So those individuals would not bring me the kinds of assurance that I would be seeking.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人不会带给我我所寻求的那种保证。

sentences.en: My hope is that we will be presented with a nominee that has a certain amount of humility and recognizes that it is not appropriate for the Supreme Court to overturn such a landmark decision.
sentences.zh: 我希望我们能迎来一位具备一定谦逊态度并认识到最高法院推翻如此具有里程碑意义的裁决是不合适的提名人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So I want to talk a little bit with you about how other people are going to be thinking about and talking about you in the coming weeks and talking to you about this process.
sentences.zh: 所以我想和您聊聊其他人将如何在接下来的几周里看待您、谈论您，以及就这个过程与您交流。

sentences.en: I imagine that the pressure is going to be enormously intense on you, starting with the president himself.
sentences.zh: 我设想您将面临巨大的压力，首先就来自总统本人。

sentences.en: And I understand that you met with him last night.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，您昨晚见了他。

sentences.en: Was it specifically about this?
sentences.zh: 是专门谈这个吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Lisa Murkowski and I were on the Senate floor and we were voting.
sentences.zh: 丽莎·穆尔科斯基和当时都在参议院大厅里，我们正在投票。

sentences.en: And all of a sudden she shows me an email message that she'd gotten from her scheduler saying that the president wanted to meet with her at 6.45 p.m.
sentences.zh: 突然她给我看了一封她从日程安排人员那里收到的电子邮件，说总统想在周四下午6点45分

sentences.en: on Thursday.
sentences.zh: 与她会面。

sentences.en: And I looked at my cell phone and sure enough, there was a message from my scheduler saying that the president wanted to meet with me at 6.30 p.m.
sentences.zh: 我看了看手机，果不其然，我的日程安排人员也发来一条消息，说总统想在6点30分与我见面。

sentences.en: So Lisa and I talked and we decided that we should go together and meet with the president.
sentences.zh: 所以丽莎和我商量了一下，我们决定一起去见总统。

sentences.en: And that's what we did.
sentences.zh: 我们就是这么做的。

sentences.en: And it was just the two of you, you and Senator Murkowski.
sentences.zh: 当时只有你们俩，你和穆尔科斯基参议员。

sentences.en: We were the only two senators, although I met other senators coming and going.
sentences.zh: 我们是仅有的两名参议员，尽管我看到其他参议员来来往往。

sentences.en: But sitting in on the meeting was the president's council and his head of legislative affairs.
sentences.zh: 但出席会议的还有总统的法律顾问和他的立法事务主管。

sentences.en: Can I imagine that because there was two of you, you got 30 minutes rather than 15?
sentences.zh: 我可以想象因为你们有两个人，所以你们得到了30分钟而不是15分钟？

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And what did you talk about, if I might ask?
sentences.zh: 如果 posso 问的话，你们谈了些什么？

sentences.en: Well, obviously, that's a nice try, but I'm not going to go into all of the details of the private conversation with the president.
sentences.zh: 好吧，很明显，这算是个不错的尝试，但我不会透露与总统私下谈话的所有细节。

sentences.en: But I did encourage him to appoint someone who could attract some Democratic support so that we did not have a partisan vote.
sentences.zh: 但我确实鼓励他任命一位能够吸引一些民主党支持的人，这样我们就不会进行党派投票。

sentences.en: And I encouraged him to appoint someone who would respect president.
sentences.zh: 我鼓励他任命一个尊重先例的人。

sentences.en: I told him that that was very important to me.
sentences.zh: 我告诉过他，这对我非常重要。

sentences.en: And what did he say in response to that?
sentences.zh: 他对此是怎么回答的呢？

sentences.en: The president was taking in all that we were saying and he listened intently.
sentences.zh: 总统认真听取了我们所说的每一句话，并且听得很专注。

sentences.en: And I also encouraged him not to feel bound by the list of potential nominees that he has put out for the public to see.
sentences.zh: 我还鼓励他不要局限于他已经向公众公布的潜在候选人名单。

sentences.en: So you encouraged him to look beyond a list that is generally populated by very conservative pro-life nominees.
sentences.zh: 所以你鼓励他超越那个通常由非常保守的、反堕胎的候选人组成的名单。

sentences.en: Well, I don't know that all of the nominees are pro-life.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我并不知道所有的候选人都是反堕胎的。

sentences.en: I do know that this list had a lot of input from the Federalist Society.
sentences.zh: 我确实知道这份名单吸收了联邦党人协会的大量意见。

sentences.en: And I believe that the president should get advice from a wide range of sources.
sentences.zh: 我相信总统应该从广泛的渠道获取建议。

sentences.en: And to be fair, also, the president, I will tell you, did say that if I had some suggestions to send them to his White House counsel.
sentences.zh: 公平地说，总统也确实对我说过，如果我有什么建议，可以发给他的白宫法律顾问。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And I assume you will.
sentences.zh: 我想你会这么做的。

sentences.en: That's a correct assumption.
sentences.zh: 这个推测很准确。

sentences.en: So the fact that the president asked to speak to you and Senator Murkowski back to back, it does suggest that, like it or not,
sentences.zh: 因此，总统相继要求与你和穆尔科斯基参议员交谈，这确实表明，不管你愿不愿意，

sentences.en: your Republican colleagues and the president himself are thinking of you as the two senators they have to focus on.
sentences.zh: 你的共和党同僚和总统本人都认为你们是他们必须重点关注的两位参议员。

sentences.en: Do you think that there's particular pressure on you and Senator Murkowski, not just because you're independent, but because you are women?
sentences.zh: 你是否认为你和穆尔科斯基参议员承受着特殊的压力，不仅仅是因为你们是独立派，而是因为你们是女性？

sentences.en: And I'm not saying that that's fair, but it may be a reality.
sentences.zh: 我并不是说这很公平，但这可能是一个现实。

sentences.en: You know, I always want to push back when people characterize positions that I take as being tied to my gender.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当人们把我的立场归结为与我的性别挂钩时，我总是想进行反驳。

sentences.en: I'm concerned about a lot of different issues, and I would resist the notion that because I am a woman, there is an extra burden on me on this particular nominee.
sentences.zh: 我关注很多不同的问题，我也反对这样一种观念：因为我是女性，我在这个特定的候选人身上就背负了额外的负担。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I want to be very clear that I'm not saying any of this is fair or right, but there's inevitably going to be a narrative here.
sentences.zh: 我想明确指出，我并不是说这一切都是公平或正确的，但这里难免会出现一种叙事。

sentences.en: A tired narrative, admittedly, where as a woman senator, if you were to support a Supreme Court justice who helped overturn Roe v.
sentences.zh: 诚然，这是一种老调重弹的叙事：作为一个女性参议员，如果你支持一个协助推翻罗诉韦德案的最高法院大法官，

sentences.en: Wade, that you would be betraying women.
sentences.zh: 你就是在背叛女性。

sentences.en: But as a Republican woman in power, you probably know better than almost anyone that there are many women who want to see Roe v.
sentences.zh: 但作为一个手握权力的共和党女性，你可能比几乎任何人都清楚，有许多女性希望看到罗诉韦德案被推翻。

sentences.en: Wade overturned.
sentences.zh: 我正想说这一点。

sentences.en: I was just going to make that very point.
sentences.zh: 你是怎么看待这一点的呢？

sentences.en: How do you think about that?
sentences.zh: 作为一个处于你这个位置的人，你是如何看待这一点的？

sentences.en: How do you think about that as somebody in your position?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，罗诉韦德案在这个国家仍然是一个高度分裂的议题。

sentences.en: You know, Roe v.
sentences.zh: 有些女性极其坚定地认为罗诉韦德案的裁决是错误的。

sentences.en: Wade is still in this country a highly divisive issue.
sentences.zh: 我也要指出，还有其他共和党女性参议员，她们在选择权问题上的看法与我和丽莎不同。

sentences.en: There are women who feel extremely strongly that Roe v.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得你不能一概而论。

sentences.en: Wade was wrongly decided.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们才是少数。

sentences.en: And I would also point out, there are other Republican women senators, and they have different views than Lisa and I do on the choice issue.
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: I just don't think you can generalize.
sentences.zh: 我们在国会的共和党女性中属于少数。

sentences.en: In fact, we're in the minority.
sentences.zh: 在支持堕胎权方面。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 在支持堕胎权方面。

sentences.en: We're in the minority among the Republican women in Congress.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是为什么这种按性别划分的现象，我真的无法理解。

sentences.en: In being pro-choice.
sentences.zh: 这是我认为尤其是许多女性深感关切的事情。

sentences.en: In being pro-choice.
sentences.zh: 但我认识的很多男性也同样非常关注这个议题。

sentences.en: So that's why this division by gender, I don't really understand.
sentences.zh: 而且在这个问题的两边都有女性。

sentences.en: It is something that I think a lot of women in particular feel strongly about.
sentences.zh: 因此，尽管你支持堕胎权，参议员，你是否认为外面有一种说法，即不支持堕胎权的女性就是在背叛其他女性，这成了一个问题？

sentences.en: But I know a lot of men who feel strongly about the issue also.
sentences.zh: 我认为确实存在这样一种说法，即不支持堕胎权的女性是在背叛其他女性。

sentences.en: And there are women on both sides of the issue.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这并不是一个公平的说法。

sentences.en: So despite being pro-choice, do you think, Senator, that it's problematic that there's a narrative out there that women who are not pro-choice are betraying other women?
sentences.zh: 我支持堕胎权，但我尊重那些与我意见不一致的人。

sentences.en: I think there is a narrative that women who are not pro-choice are betraying other women.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个非常复杂且高度私人的议题。

sentences.en: And I don't think it's a fair narrative.
sentences.zh: 我支持堕胎权的原因之一，就是我认为这是一个应该由女性个人及其家人和医生自行决定的问题。

sentences.en: I am pro-choice, but I respect those who don't agree with me.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为政府不应该进行干预，除非在非常特殊的情况下。

sentences.en: I think it's a very difficult and a very personal issue.
sentences.zh: 但这并不意味着我不尊重那些强烈反对我支持堕胎权立场的人的观点。

sentences.en: That's one reason I'm pro-choice is I think that it's an issue that should be left up to the individual woman and her family and physician.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: And I don't think government should be intervening except in extraordinary circumstances.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰。

sentences.en: But that doesn't mean that I don't respect the views of those who disagree vehemently with my pro-choice position.
sentences.zh: 我是马克·荣森。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一个专注于设计之爱及其相关文化的播客。

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin.
sentences.zh: 甚至在黑胶唱片时代我还在夜总会当DJ的时候，你每天晚上都要带300件你最珍爱的藏品去上班。

sentences.en: And I'm Mark Ronson.
sentences.zh: 你把一个DJ台变成了一个充满活力的、由美丽的50年历史艺术品组成的快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: And welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听来自爱彼的《重构者》。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl, every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用？

sentences.en: And you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 解锁版？

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 众所周知，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费体验《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用时，你在该应用中的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间去突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 如果你还不是《纽约时报》的订户，请立即下载《时报》应用，并获得30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，你在阻止梅里克·加兰的提名时，曾与党魁米奇·麦康奈尔分道扬镳，

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 当然，可以说正是这一点，才让肯尼迪大法官的离任感觉像是一个改变世界、意义重大的时刻。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 你说得对。

sentences.en: If I'm not mistaken, you broke from the party leader, Mitch McConnell, in blocking the nomination of Merrick Garland,
sentences.zh: 我不同意参议院不审议梅里克·加兰的决定，特别是当时距离大选还有好几个月，并不是只有一个月。

sentences.en: which of course is arguably what led to Justice Kennedy's departure feeling like such a world-changing, significant moment.
sentences.zh: 我相信斯卡利亚大法官是在二月份去世的，所以距离大选还有很多个月。

sentences.en: You're correct.
sentences.zh: 我与加兰法官会面了。

sentences.en: I did not agree with the decision for the Senate not to consider Merrick Garland, especially since we weren't talking about a month before the election.
sentences.zh: 我对他的印象很深，我觉得他应该经历正常的程序，我为他未能获得这一程序感到失望。

sentences.en: I believe that Justice Scalia died in February, so it was many months before the election.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，大选之后，加兰法官竟然打电话给我，感谢我对他的礼遇，

sentences.en: I met with Judge Garland.
sentences.zh: 我认为这再次证明了他是一个多么优秀的人。

sentences.en: I was impressed with him, and I felt that he deserved to go through the normal process, and I was disappointed that he didn't get that.
sentences.zh: 所以这说明你觉得司法系统正因为这种根深蒂固的党派偏见而受到损害。

sentences.en: It's interesting, after the election, Judge Garland actually called me and thanked me for my courtesy toward him,
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: which I thought was another indication of what a fine person that he is.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论最高法院的意识形态阵营时，谈论自由派阵营和保守派阵营，这让我感到非常困扰。

sentences.en: So this speaks to your feeling that the judicial system is being compromised by this deep partisanship.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》曾做过一项分析，关于自由派阵营的投票一致性与保守派阵营的凝聚力相比如何。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，这不是法官应该采取的方法。

sentences.en: It bothers me deeply that we speak of ideological blocs on the Supreme Court, that we talk about the liberal bloc, and we talk about the conservative bloc.
sentences.zh: 他们应该抛开意识形态和个人观点，将法律和宪法应用于案件的事实。

sentences.en: And the New York Times has done an analysis on how often the liberal bloc votes together versus the conservative bloc's cohesion.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当我采访加兰法官时，我问他，你的司法哲学是什么？

sentences.en: And to me, that's not the approach that judges should be taking.
sentences.zh: 他的回答让我感到高兴。

sentences.en: They should put aside their ideological and personal views and apply the law and the Constitution to the facts of the case.
sentences.zh: 他说，我没有司法哲学。

sentences.en: In fact, when I interviewed Judge Garland, I asked him, what is your judicial philosophy?
sentences.zh: 你对此表示欢迎，因为这意味着他不会归入其中某一个阵营。

sentences.en: And he gave me a response which delighted me.
sentences.zh: 正确。

sentences.en: He said, I don't have a judicial philosophy.
sentences.zh: 参议员，听到你这样谈论最高法院很有意思，因为我认为这也是我们看待你目前所在的这个机构——参议院的方式，

sentences.en: Which you welcomed, because it meant he wouldn't fit into one of those blocs or the other.
sentences.zh: 议员们都在泾渭分明、可靠的意识形态阵营中投票。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 而如今你被认为是其中的罕见例外。

sentences.en: It's interesting, Senator, to hear you talk this way about the Supreme Court, because I think this is also how we think about the body you serve in right now, the Senate,
sentences.zh: 诚然，在我有幸在参议院服务的这些年里，这里的党派性越来越强了。

sentences.en: that members vote in clear, reliable ideological blocs.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也不是一个健康的现象。

sentences.en: And you are considered the rare exception to that these days.
sentences.zh: 但我将立法机构与司法机构，或者行政机构与司法机构区分开来。

sentences.en: It's certainly true that in the years that I've been privileged to serve in the Senate, that it has become increasingly partisan.
sentences.zh: 尽管已经走到了极端，但每个人都期望国会就其本质而言是带有党派色彩的。

sentences.en: And I don't think that's a healthy development either.
sentences.zh: 行政机构也是如此。

sentences.en: But I distinguish between the legislative branch and the judiciary or the executive branch and the judiciary.
sentences.zh: 但在我看来，司法机构本该凌驾于纯粹的党派政治之上。

sentences.en: Everyone expects, even though it's gone to an extreme, for Congress to be partisan by its very nature.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我感到担忧：无论是确认司法提名人的过程，

sentences.en: And the same with the executive branch.
sentences.zh: 还是我们在最高法院的判决中看到的日益极化的趋势，似乎都在变得越来越糟糕。

sentences.en: But to me, the judicial branch is supposed to be above raw partisan politics.
sentences.zh: 但是，鉴于你刚刚描述的当前政治现状，你认为有哪怕一丝可能，

sentences.en: And that's why I'm concerned that both the process of confirming nominees to the judiciary,
sentences.zh: 这次最高法院的提名程序不会成为我们见过的关于谁能获得该席位的最极端的政治斗争吗？

sentences.en: as well as the increasing polarization we see in decisions coming out of the Supreme Court, are trends that seem to be getting worse.
sentences.zh: 嗯，希望总是存在的，但我并不乐观，这绝对会是一场真正的恶战。

sentences.en: But do you think it's even remotely possible, given the current state of politics that you've just described,
sentences.zh: 但我感到非常困扰的是，两党中我的同僚和朋友们甚至在还没有提名人之前就已经宣布了立场。

sentences.en: that this Supreme Court nomination process will not be the most extreme political fight we've ever seen over who gets that Supreme Court slot?
sentences.zh: 这太不可思议了。

sentences.en: Well, hope springs eternal, but I am not optimistic that it will be other than a real battle.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: But I'm very troubled that my colleagues and friends on both sides of the aisle have already announced positions before there even is a nominee.
sentences.zh: 没有比人们似乎已经开始排兵布阵更明显的迹象表明这将是一个政治化过程和政治决定了。

sentences.en: That's extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 他们已经在为一个尚未选出的提名人进行反对或强烈支持的站队了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 这种程度的现象我以前从未见过。

sentences.en: There's no clearer sign that this would be a political process and a political decision than the fact that people already seem to be putting themselves in camps.
sentences.zh: 你可能也知道这一点。

sentences.en: They're already lining up, either in opposition or in strong support for a nominee who has not yet been chosen.
sentences.zh: 你现在正被拿来与安东尼·肯尼迪作比较，而你很快将不得不批准或否决他的继任者。

sentences.en: That I have never seen before to this extent.
sentences.zh: 你们都被视为在意识形态上独立，并且能够与你们的政党保持距离。

sentences.en: You probably know this.
sentences.zh: 从我们的角度来看，你确实和肯尼迪大法官有很多共同点，因为他作为那个关键的摇摆票拥有如此巨大的影响力。

sentences.en: You're being compared right now to the Supreme Court justice whose replacement you're going to have to approve or reject pretty soon, Anthony Kennedy.
sentences.zh: 而且因为他不盲从任何特定的路线，你是否觉得在接替肯尼迪大法官的事情上，你拥有真正的力量？

sentences.en: You're both seen as ideologically independent and capable of standing apart from your party.
sentences.zh: 我并不在寻求权力。

sentences.en: From where we sit, it certainly looks like you have a lot in common with Justice Kennedy because he had so much power in being that swing vote.
